questions.question_text: After a $16\%$ increase, a train fare is $\$29$. Find the fare before the increase.

options.why: Took $16\%$ off $\$29$ instead of dividing by $116\%$; the old fare is not $84\%$ of the new one.
Increased $\$29$ by a further $16\%$ instead of working backwards.
Found $16\%$ of $\$29$, the size of the rise, rather than the original fare.

questions.question_text: After a $40\%$ decrease, a flight ticket costs $\$276$. Find the original price.

options.why: Added $40\%$ of $\$276$ instead of dividing by $60\%$; the original is not $140\%$ of the new price.
Took a further $40\%$ off $\$276$ instead of working backwards.
Found $40\%$ of $\$276$, the size of the drop, rather than the original price.

questions.question_text: The number of daily passengers on a bus route fell by $30\%$, a drop of $42$ passengers. How many passengers were there each day originally?

options.why: Treated the $42$ as the $70\%$ still travelling instead of as the $30\%$ lost.
Gave the number still travelling, which is $70\%$, rather than the original number.
Found $30\%$ of $42$ instead of scaling $42$ up from $30\%$ to $100\%$.

questions.solution_text:
The drop of $42$ passengers is the $30\%$ decrease.
$30\% = 42$
$1\% = 42 \div 30 = 1.4$
$100\% = 1.4 \times 100$
$= 140$ passengers

questions.question_text: After a $12\%$ pay rise, a worker earns $\$168$ a day. A student finds the original pay by taking $12\%$ off $\$168$, getting $\$147.84$. Is this correct?

options.text: No; the original was $\$150$, because $\$168$ is $112\%$ of the original, not $100\%$.
Yes; taking $12\%$ off reverses a $12\%$ increase exactly.
options.why: A $12\%$ increase and a $12\%$ decrease act on different amounts, so they do not cancel.

options.text: No; the original was $\$188.16$, found by adding $12\%$ to $\$168$.
options.why: Adds another increase instead of working back to $100\%$.

options.text: Yes; $\$147.84$ is $88\%$ of $\$168$, which is the original.
options.why: The original is $100\%$ of itself, not $88\%$ of the increased value.
